To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

auditory brainstem neurons involved with sound source localization have several morphological and biochemical features to compute interaurial level and time differences, and that synaptic transmission in these auditory synapses is reliable and temporally accurate even during sustained periods with high‐rate activity.

the auditory brainstem synapses, which are involved in sound source localisation, are equipped with molecular and morphological features that enable them (i) to compute interaurally different sound levels and time delays, and (ii) to reliably transmit information at a high rate for prolonged periods of time, and (iii) to do so with a temporal precision in the range of milliseconds.
the auditory brainstem synapses have a higher quantal content and replenishment than the hippocampal ones.

the mechanisms that allow neurons in the auditory brainstem to compute interaurally encoded sound source localization cues.
understanding how the auditory system is able to compute interaurally derived sound source cues.
understanding the mechanisms that enable auditory brainstem neurons to reliably compute interaural time differences and to transmit this information to the brainstem nuclei.

the auditory brainstem is the most reliable and most precise synapse in the central nervous system.
auditory synapses are equipped with several features that allow them to operate reliably and precisely even during sustained high‐rate activity.
the high‐frequency auditory synapses have evolved to provide the necessary temporal precision for sound source localization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the high quantal content of the auditory synapses is a major factor for the high synaptic reliability and temporal fidelity of auditory brainstem neurons.
auditory synapses are equipped with a number of molecular, morphological, and functional features that allow them to perform at high‐speed and reliably.
the auditory brainstem is a highly specialized system for sound source localization and that the synaptic properties we report here are a reflection of that.

synaptic properties are adapted to the specific demands of the respective neural circuit.
the auditory brainstem has evolved to be able to perform sound localization in an efficient way.
synaptic transmission is not a one size fits all solution but is adapted to the specific needs of the synapse and the network in which it resides.
